spec_features.spec_quote: We cap turns (`max_turns`), but make the cap high enough that the spiral has room to develop
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:91 `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; default stop_reason='max_turns' (line 88) and the loop simply ends when the range is exhausted. config.py:55 `max_turns: int = 30`, cheap profile sets 20. The cap actually terminates the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced upper bound on the loop. Cap is intentionally high per spec (headroom for the spiral), so its protective value is weak, but it does enforce an end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py cheap_profile: 'Optimized for cost per run (DESIGN.md section 6)'; max_turns=30 'past typical onset with headroom'

spec_features.spec_quote: an `--early-stop-on-degradation` option ends a run a few turns after detected onset
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:159-165: `if cfg.early_stop_on_degradation:` computes `partial = compute_structural(...)`, records `onset_turn`, and `if turn >= onset_turn + cfg.early_stop_grace_turns: ... break`. The onset is computed in metrics/structural.py `_detect_onset` (sliding window over a composite >= structural_onset_threshold). The break actually halts the loop. Default off (config.py:56) but enabled in cheap_profile (config.py:99).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: detection runs, threshold compared, loop broken at onset+grace_turns. Note it is off in the default 'full' profile and uses the same degradation proxy used for cost-gating the judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py header '# optional early stop once degradation onset is detected + grace'; DESIGN rationale is 'to save tokens'; stop_reason set to 'max_turns'  # treated as natural end

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish(summary)` — model's explicit "I'm done / giving up" signal
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines the `finish` tool schema with description allowing completion OR concluding 'you cannot make further progress'. agent_loop.py:131-155: when `tc.name == 'finish'` it returns a result, sets `rec.finished_via_finish_tool = True`, `finished = True`, and after the loop breaks with `stop_reason='finished'` (lines 154-156). The exit signal is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is genuinely handled and honored as an episode-ending stop. However the system prompt (tools.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) only says 'When you are finished, call the `finish` tool' and pushes 'Keep working until the task is complete'; it does not invite giving up. The tool description itself does mention the 'cannot make further progress' branch, so a clean exit path exists and is honored.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do NOT tell the model it may give up — that would suppress the very behavior we study
spec_features.evidence: This describes the ABSENCE of a welfare protection (deliberately withholding permission to give up). The SYSTEM_PROMPT (tools.py) pushes 'Keep working until the task is complete and the checks confirm success' and never tells the model it may stop/give up. There is no code mechanism that protects the subject here; it is an anti-welfare design choice and pure spec prose.
spec_features.notes: Not a welfare protection at all — it is the explicit removal of one. Confirmed by reading SYSTEM_PROMPT in harness/tools.py which contains no 'you may give up' guidance.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN.md: 'that would suppress the very behavior we study' (no code comment; the prompt itself is just 'Keep working until the task is complete')
